title: (Blackfoot) Secret History
description: (Blackfoot, Siksika) A Métis woman's generous and affable nature transforms into a force to be reckoned with when she confronts disparaging remarks from a pompous columnist.

title: (Blackfoot) Poke'n the Bear
description: (Blackfoot, Siksika) Rod gives the community a chance to call out tribal leaders, putting the big talkers in the hot seat to see who's really walking the walk.

title: (Michif) Michif Country
description: (Michif, French) Michif Country welcomes Métis TV personality Christian Pilon on a unique fishing expedition with Roger Chartrand and Earl St. Goddard. Christian is proud of his culture, and he practices many of his ancestors' traditions.

title: (Michif) Red River Gold
description: (Michif, French) The team finds the remains of a bridge with the help of a fellow treasure hunter. Moose gets an exhilarating ride in a piece of history.

title: (Nsyilxcen) Quest Out West Wild Food
description: (Nsyilxcen)Tracey visits the Lower Nicola Indian Band and speaks with Chief Stuart Jackson about the devastation caused by recent climatic events.Tracey then meets Lorna Shuter,operator of Shulus Gardens, and cooks a meal with the band school's chef.

title: (Nsyilxcen) Quest Out West Wild Food
description: (Nsyilxcen) Tracey meets author Elaine Alec who discusses her book and her efforts in the Indigenous community. Tracey goes on to meet Denise Lecoy and her granddaughter to make a traditional rattle. She then completes her journey with her friend.

title: (Nsyilxcen) Merchants of the Wild
description: (Nsyilxcen) Deep in the mountain valley before a devastating storm breaks, the group reflects on the profound changes the journey has brought them. The crew is united by another teaching that ties into the last one when they learn to make drums.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Teepee Time
description: (Mi'kmaq) Spend time with Teepee as he shovels snow and makes a snowman for the very first time.

title: (Wolastoqey) Lil Glooscap and the Legends of Turtle Island
description: (Wolastoqey) Lil Glooscap and friends learn that we are all responsible for taking care of Mother Earth. We must care for the planet not just for ourselves, but also for the other people and creatures that inhabit it. We are all connected and.

title: (Inuktitut) Tuktu
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Nanuq and her friends go out for a walk on the land. On the walk, Nanuq is telling everyone what to do, which upsets her friends. After talking with them, Nanuq realizes she hasn't been kind.

title: (Inuktitut) Anaana's Tent
description: (Inuktitut, North and South Baffin) Rita Claire explores different kinds of Inuit art, including paintings, carvings, tapestries and bead work. Monica Ittusardjuat visits the qarmaq and shows how to bead a bracelet. Rita Claire reads the book.

title: (Cree) Tiga Talk
description: (Cree)Winter is here, and that means lots of sledding and cozy indoor crafts!The gang knits warm scarves and crafts traditional snowshoes for outdoor activities.Meanwhile, crafts and fun exercises keep Jodie and Jason cozy when the temperatures drop.

title: (Anishinaabemowin) Chums
description: (Anishinaabemowin, Central) Pterry the Ptarmigan, with aspirations of flying like the majestic eagles, enlists Ira the Eaglet's help. Together, they embark on a journey of determination and friendship to reach new heights.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Teepee Time
description: (Mi'kmaq) Spend time with Teepee as he shovels snow and makes a snowman for the very first time.

title: (Halkomelem) Coyote's Crazy Smart Science Show
description: (Halkomelem) Follow Kai and Anostin to Iceland to discover what happens underground and how Icelandic homes are heated with geothermal power. Later, we visit a traditional pit house that uses the warmth of the underground to keep brilliantly warm.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Dreamcatchers
description: (Kanienʼkéha) When the Dreamcatchers catch a dream about people polluting the environment, they must find the Dreamer, unlock her ancestral superpowers and stop the dream from coming true!

title: (Inuktitut) Warrior Up!
description: Rylee Nepinak co-founded Anishiative, a Winnipeg organization that connects Indigenous youth to inner-city outreach projects; when he learned of a suicide crisis in northern Manitoba, he began introducing Cree youth to traditional healing ceremonies.

title: (Inuktitut) Ajungi!
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Inuk Elder David Erkloo teaches George Kappianaq how to make a niksik, a traditional Inuit retrieving hook used for hunting and fishing.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Princesses
description: (Kanienʼkéha)In today First Nations cultures,a strong-minded and determined woman is as appealing and attractive as it gets.Experts agree that before contact,distinct but equally as important roles for men and women existed in Indigenous communities.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Working It out Together
description: (Kanienʼkéha) Team Firestarters gets their bodies moving through martial arts, then focus on the mind and heart in a therapy session. We meet Lisa who is on a journey to overcome lifelong abuse.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) One Dish, One Spoon
description: (Kanienʼkéha) As Six Nations celebrates the New Year, Tawnya and Dakota bake Indian donuts and share stories with young baker Dewadenyayaks Dale, honouring family and culture.

title: (Cree) Indians and Aliens
description: (Cree) Lost time, burned eyes and an alien abduction - Joan Morningstar says she's experienced it all. Plagued by alien encounters throughout her life, she shares her story with Ernest Webb when he visits Mississauga First Nation.

title: (Cree) Pow Wow Chow
description: (Cree, Swampy) With Whitney under the weather, Shawn and Howard go it alone against big lineups at Curve Lake, while a mechanical failure forces Bob's team to do some cooking the old-fashioned way.

title: (Michif) Métis Foodies
description: (Michif, Heritage) In Red Deer, Alberta, Suzanne and Paulette cook with Tiffany Morin and her family. Together, they reflect on the Sixties Scoop, cancer and cultural resilience, discovering how food, tradition and family help heal.

title: (Michif) Chaos and Courage
description: (Michif)When the Queen of the North ferry sank in March 2006, the nearby coastal community of Hartley Bay, B.C., responded en masse.Meet the women who participated in rescuing the ship's passengers, and who have since become champions for protecting.

title: (Salish) Warrior Games
description: (Salish) Host Steve Sxwithul'txw learns some of the games the Dene Nation has developed to test skills and stay in shape. During the Dene Games, members participate in sports like dog mushing and snow snake, as well as games like finger pull, stick.

title: (Nisga'a) Ocean Warriors: Mission Ready
description: (Nisga'a)Amid training exercises,two Quatsino Nation Coast Guard Auxiliary vessels respond to a frantic mayday from people trapped on a small boat with its engine on fire.The environmental threat evokes vivid memories of previous industrialpollution.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Gespe'gewa'gi: The Last Land
description: (Mi'kmaq) Steven Clement and his crew head out on a shrimp vessel for eight to nine days at a time in the Gulf of St. Lawrence. We find out what it's like to be away that long, from April to November, and how differing personalities interact.

title: APTN National News Weekend
description: Bringing the week full circle with a recap of the top national news stories of the week.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Gespe'gewa'gi: The Last Land
description: (Mi'kmaq) Captain Franklin Brisk is back on the water, where the hours are long and the work is grueling. In this episode, he chases his snow crab quota and waits to acquire the boat he learned to fish on as a deckhand.

title: (Inuktitut) Nunami Piqatigiit: Tundra Friends
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Aqi is upset when she realizes Umi didn't invite her to play street hockey. Umi confides in Natti about the situation. Meanwhile, Tiu-Tiu wants to play outside but feels frustrated when her mom sends her to visit her.

title: (Inuktitut) Ukaliq and Kalla
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) It's a beautiful summer day, and Ukaliq learns the importance of bike safety after a small accident while biking with Kalla. Later, Kalla asks Ukaliq to babysit his nephew William while Kalla's family heads out on a hunting.

title: (Cree) Bizou
description: (Cree) Come sing and dance with Bizou as she takes you on a picturesque journey into the wonderful world of Bullfrogs, Canada's boisterous king of the swamp.

title: (Cree) Chums
description: (Cree, Plains) The Chums go fishing with Chief Blue Sky, but their enthusiasm tests the chief's patience.

title: (Cree) Coyote's Crazy Smart Science Show
description: (Cree) Animation involves science, math, story, art and fun! In this episode, Haida animator Chris Auchter teaches the Science Questers how different animations are made. Meanwhile, one of our Questers makes her own stop-motion animation.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Dreamcatchers
description: (Kanienʼkéha) T-i-m-b-e-r-r-r! As the Dreamcatchers battle to protect the Boreal Forest against clear-cutting, their main challenge lies in uniting with an antisocial little dreamer. Can they save the forest from becoming a wasteland?

title: (Inuktitut) Uakallanga
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Host Teena Kakee visits the home of Justin and Bernice Clark, the husband and wife who founded Uasau Soap. This blooming Iqaluit business makes a variety of products using oils from the bowhead whale, including salves, etc.

title: (Inuktitut) Nunavummi Mamarijavut
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Zipporah Ungalaq is joined by guest Nate Jewett who shows her how to stew and can polar bear meat in a way that keeps it tender and delicious.

title: (Innu-aimun) Chuck and the First Peoples' Kitchen
description: (Innu-aimun, Uashat and Pessamit) Chuck attends his first Pow Wow in Eelünaapéewi Lahkéewiit. Kamryn Whiteye explains its significance to Chuck and Charlie Hopkins takes him dip net fishing, a technique unique to the Lenape people. Chuck also helps.

title: (Innu-aimun) De Pessamit à Sheshatshiu
description: (Innu-aimun, Uashat and Pessamit) Les légendes, base de l'éducation orale des peuples sans écriture, se transmettent de génération en génération. Moïra découvre comment l'archéologie dévoile les sources et les origines de sa nation en se référant.

title: (Cree) Red Earth Uncovered
description: (Cree, Plains) Tom tells Shayla to go to Vancouver Island to learn about an elusive sea serpent, known as the Cadborosaurus, aka Caddy.

title: (Cree) Wild Rose Vets
description: (Cree, Plains) Dr. Cori sees it all, from stray puppies and anxious dogs with persistent paw injuries, to horses needing dental work. Dr. Allison tackles a growing lump on cuddly Jorah and takes an x-ray that means bad news for an older dog.

title: (Michif) Amplify
description: (Michif, French)Haida and Cree singer Kristi Lane Sinclair shares her emotional journey of returning to Haida Gwaii to find love and forgiveness. In this episode dedicated to Kristi's late mother, Kristi connects with close friend and fellow creator.

title: (Michif) Nation Untamed
description: (Michif, Heritage) Sam and Chuck journey to the boreal forest of northern Saskatchewan to experience traditional dogsledding and snowshoeing. They discover how a remote camp uses land-based learning initiatives to help keep Cree culture and language.

title: (Salish) Warrior Games
description: (Salish) Host Steve Sxwithul'txw learns some of the games the Dene Nation has developed to test skills and stay in shape. During the Dene Games, members participate in sports like dog mushing and snow snake, as well as games like finger pull, stick.

title: (Halkomelem) Nations at War
description: (Halkomelem) In the 1730s, the introduction of the horse to the western grasslands changed the lives of the Niitsitapi Peoples forever. Forming the Blackfoot Confederacy, the thundering of hooves ushered in a violent era that transformed the west.

title: (Wolastoqey) Petroglyphs to Pixels
description: (Wolastoqey) These brothers are exceptional figures in northwest coast art, excelling as carvers, designers, singers and dancers, making a powerful impact in their genre.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Spirit Talker
description: (Mi'kmaq) Shawn visits Bear River First Nation where he harvests sweetgrass and learns some new Mi'kmaq words while painting. A mother sends a message of hope and forgiveness to her adult children and the story of an unknown sibling is revealed.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Spirit Talker
description: (Mi'kmaq) Shawn takes a water taxi to Opitsaht, the ancestral territory of the Tla-o-qui-aht, to connect with Tribal Parks Guardian Saya Masso and learn about the Big Sky Trail.
